thread:
marta: Heads-up — during the eu canary we saw a burst of tenant writes landing in eu-west even though their pinned residency is us-east. Some requests got 503s when forwarding queue filled. I want to propose a small arbitration surface for writes that land in non-resident regions

james: ouch. can you sketch the proposal? latency / correctness tradeoffs matter a lot here :thinking:

olivia: high-level: attempt short sync-forward to resident region (synchronous proxy), wait up to N ms, then either 1) place an escrowed write (queued with cidempotency) or 2) return a 429/503 with a clear consumer-level hint. Prefer option 1 for PLG UX.

marta: exactly. details: default max_wait_ms=150, escrow TTL=30s, escrow persists to local durable queue + async-retry to resident. If forwarding succeeds -> return normal 200.

infra-bot: deploy started: feature/regional-forwarding-v1 -> canary -> eu-west (triggered by @marta)

sanjay: careful about ordering. If we escrow and later replay to resident, we must preserve causality for a tenant's concurrent writes. How do we guarantee no reordering compared to reads?

li: idea: attach a forwarding-serial-token header with each forwarded/escrowed write. Resident apply path will use token to place write after last_seen_seq for that tenant. If missing sequence, resident can re-fetch or stall.

olivia: that's workable but increases coupling. Alternative: optimistic apply in eu-west with provisional flag and readers in eu prefer resident unless provisional allowed. But that leaks PII across region boundaries — legal says no for some tenants.

jas: legal/regulatory: we must enforce per-tenant policy: some tenants are "no-cross-border" -> no forwarding allowed, must return an explicit error and surface a retry-to-resident hint to client. Others are relaxed and can use escrow/forward. Put this rule in tenant profile at config-time.

marta: agreed. default policy = allow-forwarding-with-escrow. tenant override enforced by proxy ACL.

emma: telemetry checklist: add metrics for forwarded_count, forward_latency_p50/p99, escrow_queued, escrow_replay_success, escrow_replay_failure. Add trace tag for tenant_policy and whether forwarded or escrowed.

james: can we make drift-safe fallback? if resident is overloaded and forwarding keeps failing, maybe auto-failover to local-only with writes quarantined and ops page notified? We need operator circuit-breaker thresholds.

marta: yes — operator policy: if resident overload rate > 30% for 2m and forwarded failure rate > 10% then flip tenant to "quarantine-local" mode and require manual review. We'll surface a runbook link.

li: quick config snippet for the proxy behavior:

```yaml
regional_forwarding:
  max_wait_ms: 150
  escrow_ttl_s: 30
  mode: sync_then_escrow  # options: sync_then_escrow, sync_only, escrow_only, block
  tenant_policies:
    allow_cross_border: true/false
    auto_quarantine_thresholds:
      resident_overload_pct: 30
      forward_fail_pct: 10
```

marta: thanks li — we'll iterate. Next steps: write a tiny RFC addendum that covers: 1) wire header semantics (forward-token, tenant-policy-hint), 2) escrow durability guarantees and retry backoff, 3) metrics/tracing, 4) operator flip triggers + runbook. I can draft and drop in #architecture-rfcs.

jas: add a legal sign-off checkbox for tenant profiles that permit forwarding. We should also include an audit log event when forwarding occurs.

olivia: one more concern: prefix/KV cache invalidation. If we forward but readers go to eu-west cache, they might read stale. Proposed: tag provisional writes with a short-lived cache-invalidation event via pubsub so edge caches in region get a TTL bump.

marta: noted. we'll include a pubsub-invalidation step as optional (opt-in via tenant policy).

sanjay: test plan: k6 load with artificial resident latency injected; assert no data loss for 10000 writes with mix of policies, assert quarantine flip under overload, assert GDPR tenants never forward.

marta: perfect. thanks all — I'll draft RFC addendum and ping for reviews.

emma: :thumbsup: leave the canary on for a few hours and watch forward_lat_p99.

li: tagging ops @sre for runbook review once draft exists.

marta: done. I'll create the RFC in ~30m and post link here when ready.
